A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same theoretical research work, with readable text, equations, proofs and references. All pages support comparison; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, proofs and analytical examples, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 likewise contains theoretical results and illustrative constructions. Its revised Section 6 introduces no empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same approximate per-domain error access and min-max ERM predictor in Equations (2)–(3). No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Neither version reports training or evaluation on datasets or benchmarks. The illustrative tasks and theoretically constructed distributions are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version contains experimentally evaluated baselines. The analytical comparison with standard ERM in Remark 4.3 is unchanged; the added citations are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol is added or revised. The theoretical sampling setup, error definitions and sample requirements remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablation, robustness or supplementary empirical analyses. Remark 4.3 and Examples 6.1–6.2 retain their analytical examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars or significance tests. The probability guarantees and concentration arguments are unchanged theoretical material.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are present in either version. The numerical toy examples, analytical bounds and qualitative findings are retained.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions and theorem bounds are unchanged. Theorem 6.1's proof introduces covering-neighborhood notation and restates the same non-shattering and counting argument. Its strict inequalities and explicit cover-transfer observation elaborate mathematics already established in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 retain the same domain sample-complexity characterization, min-max ERM guarantee, near-matching lower bound and tight relationship with VC dimension.

C2.justification: Section 6 now explicitly explains that ordinary H-divergence covers suffice and interprets the retained refined-divergence bound as stronger. This clarifies applicability without changing the result. Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed. Section 4.1's description of estimating errors from per-domain samples is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds Schölkopf et al. (2012), Zhang et al. (2015) and Gong et al. (2016), with corresponding references and a sentence identifying their causal assumptions. This modestly broadens the prior-work discussion.

P1.justification: Section 6 receives localized explanatory and proof rewriting, alongside the added related-work sentence and small wording corrections. The section ordering and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Theorem 6.1's final displayed proof inequality becomes an inline conclusion, and nearby prose and references reflow. Neither version contains figures or tables; the overall page format is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's terse partition argument, v2's explicit covering neighborhoods make Theorem 6.1 easier to follow and verify. The clearer domain-adaptation connection and added causal prior work provide modest gains in exposition and context. The central guarantees and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
